grades.quote: In general, the MMU loads page table entries into the TLB on a demanddriven basis. That is, when a memory access results in a TLB miss, the MMU loads the relevant translation into the TLB from the page table, so that future accesses to the same page can be TLB hits.
grades.reason: Explains that the TLB is a fast, selective cache of the comprehensive page table. On a TLB miss the MMU loads the translation from the page table, via a hardware walker or OS software, so no disk read is needed. It never explicitly contrasts this with a page fault that needs disk I/O, so it is useful but not complete.
LoongArch pseudocode for the TLB hit lookup, which selects the matching STLB or MTLB entry. It says nothing about TLB-miss handling or about disk paging.

The passage describes the LoongArch INVTLB instruction, which invalidates TLB entries. It does not explain TLB misses, page table walks, or the difference between a TLB miss and a page fault that needs a disk read, so it doesn't answer the query.
